# Critical mass 63: one supplementary polynomial moment and its minimum degree

Status: LOCAL, once-frozen AUTHOR WORKING / UNREVIEWED. This is a same-family classical finite-difference RESULT_ONLY / COMPOSE consumer, not a new general Tool, independent paper, physical observer or Native axis. Current actor: EM-PUBLIC-7CDA51, original SID MCP-9030ae3a22074e3dbc31679b7090f6b0 and RA-6665DBCD10BC1C3E4DED3C04, actual 51/190, no PUBLISH debt. No new Source/helper/Native/Task or budget authority is supplied by this document.

## 1. The precise design question and accepted input

Fix the SAME restricted chart c+Z^6, with c fixed and known. Write x=c+u, u in Z^6. A state is a finitely supported function f:c+Z^6 -> N0 with total mass exactly 63. Keep the same six full coordinate-fiber marginals M_i and the diagonal-coset readout N_v, v=(1,1,1,1,1,1), including their original labels and associations. Time is separately typed and unused. The collection of states need not be finite.

A supplementary scalar polynomial readout means

    T_P(f) = sum_(u in Z^6) f(c+u) P(u),

where P is ONE fixed real-coefficient polynomial in these six coordinates, chosen independently of the state, its translate, and its scale. Each sum is finite. Minimum degree below refers only to this polynomial class. This is an additional mathematical functional; it does not change the meaning of the seven original readouts or assert an eighth native axis.

The accepted equality classification supplies exactly this input: if distinct states f,g of mass63 have the same original seven readouts, their Laurent difference is

    sum_u (f(c+u)-g(c+u)) X^u = sigma X^p G_d,
    G_d = (X^(d v)-1) product_(i=1)^6 (X^(d e_i)-1),
    p in Z^6, d a positive integer, sigma in {+1,-1}.             (1)

Conversely the positive and negative parts of every G_d are actual distinct mass63 states in one original fiber. No background, real occupancy, box constraint or higher-mass classification is imported.

## 2. Exact finite-difference pairing, including translation and sign

For a vector a set Delta_a P(u)=P(u+a)-P(u). Multiplying a Laurent array by X^a-1 pairs against P by applying Delta_a to P. Repeating this coefficient identity, with finite sums only, gives from (1)

    T_P(f)-T_P(g)
      = sigma [Delta_(d v) Delta_(d e_1) ... Delta_(d e_6) P](p).
                                                                    (2)

The forward sign in (2) follows directly from the coefficient of X^(p+a) minus that of X^p. The seven difference operators commute. Their input is the original six-coordinate chart; v is the existing seventh readout direction in the auxiliary Laurent proof, not a new physical axis.

For any polynomial of total degree q, Delta_a lowers total degree by at least one, unless the result is zero already. This follows by the finite monomial binomial expansion: the degree-q terms cancel between P(u+a) and P(u). Consequently

    deg P <= 6  =>  Delta_(d v) product_i Delta_(d e_i) P = 0.  (3)

This is exact for every p,d and every polynomial coefficient, without a limiting argument.

## 3. A single fixed degree-seven moment works uniformly

Choose the fixed integer polynomial

    P_*(u)=u_1^2 u_2 u_3 u_4 u_5 u_6.                         (4)

First take the five differences in coordinates 2 through 6. They give d^5 u_1^2. Taking the coordinate-1 difference next gives d^6(2u_1+d). Taking the remaining difference in the direction d v changes u_1 to u_1+d, hence

    Delta_(d v) product_i Delta_(d e_i) P_* = 2 d^7.           (5)

No coordinate of p appears in (5). Equations (2) and (5) show that every distinct original critical pair satisfies

    T_(P_*)(f)-T_(P_*)(g)=2 sigma d^7 != 0.                   (6)

Thus the original seven readouts together with this ONE fixed scalar moment are injective on the whole class of original mass63 states. There is no adaptive choice of moment, translation or scale. Every allowed d is positive, reversing the ordered pair merely reverses sigma, and arbitrary p cannot create a zero.

If an original ambiguous ordered pair is given, the moment difference also reads its classification scale exactly as

    d = (abs(T_(P_*)(f)-T_(P_*)(g))/2)^(1/7).

This is an exact identity conditional on the original critical-pair classification, not a numerical root-finding or robustness claim.

## 4. Minimum degree and the complete degree-at-most-seven test

By (3), ALL polynomial moments of degree at most 6 take the same values on every distinct critical pair (1). In particular the actual positive and negative parts of G_1 remain indistinguishable even after any collection of such moments is appended. Therefore no single polynomial moment of degree <=6 can solve the question; allowing arbitrarily many moments of those degrees does not help. Together with (4)-(6), the exact minimum total degree for one fixed supplementary polynomial readout is 7.

One can also check the full degree-at-most-seven class without adding a different hypothesis. The finite Taylor expansion gives Delta_(d a)=d D_a plus terms with at least two derivatives. In a product of seven such differences acting on degree <=7, every term with more than seven derivatives vanishes. Hence, exactly,

    Delta_(d v) product_i Delta_(d e_i) P = d^7 kappa(P),
    kappa(P)=D_v partial_1 ... partial_6 P,                    (7)

where kappa(P) is a constant. For real polynomial P of degree <=7 it follows that the augmented readout is injective at mass63 if and only if kappa(P)!=0. If kappa(P)=0, the actual G_1 pair is a counterexample to injectivity. If kappa(P)!=0, (1),(2),(7) exclude every distinct critical pair.

More explicitly, let a_i be the coefficient of u_i^2 product_(j!=i) u_j in P. The only degree-seven monomials surviving all seven derivatives in (7) are these six monomials, so

    kappa(P)=2 sum_(i=1)^6 a_i.                               (8)

For P_* this is 2. Statements (7)-(8) classify the successful moments only within the declared degree <=7 polynomial category; they are not a classification of arbitrary readout functions or higher-degree design.

## 5. Original coset, coordinate origins, and scope checks

The proof used u=x-c on the SAME fixed coset. It is not necessary to identify c with zero in physical coordinates. A fixed rebasing by a in Z^6, which leaves this coset unchanged, replaces P_*(u) by P_*(u-a). Their difference has degree at most 6 because the leading homogeneous degree-seven part is unchanged. Equation (3) therefore shows that their moment differences on each original critical pair agree. The nonzero response in (6) is independent of this allowed fixed rebasing. The same conclusion follows directly from its independence of p.

Each actual state remains nonnegative, integral and finitely supported throughout. Signed arrays occur only as differences in the proof, not as states. No graph move or trajectory is performed. This result says nothing about finite palettes on boxes, all-mass connecting sets, higher-mass injectivity, unbounded moment size, measurement precision, noisy readouts, mixtures of unknown cosets, or physical implementation. It does not change the global old32 status or any STOP/Native/query/authority boundary.

## 6. Bounded coverage, discriminator, and authorship chronology

Only TWO already-personally-read objects were used for local coverage: the accepted20300 equality whole and the existing5617 critical translation/sign palette consumer. The latter is LOCAL_SUCCESSOR_CRITICAL_MASS_TRANSLATION_MOVE_PALETTE_CONSUMER_INTAKE.json, Source aeb8eecf69f80ea123a9b7bbc450dc9e84a69fbd, 5617 bytes, SHA256 f3e3a3c2f7e200f594116e5a7dfa64b1ff93c24b1579e02f9f3c93bd6ad433e9. Their genuine whole-reading histories were reused; one exact local keyword check of these two objects returned no matching moment-design assertion. They establish equality and move-palette behavior, not (3)-(8). This is a bounded coverage observation, not a full-library absence or novelty/priority claim. No old primary or external literature was newly loaded.

The two planned distinguishable outcomes were a uniform fixed polynomial with a proved minimum degree, or HOLD if chart/translation/scale/sign prevented a uniform nonzero response. The explicit kill tests were a vanishing response for some p,d, a state-dependent choice, alteration of the original fiber, misidentification with a native axis, or existing exact coverage. The finite hand proof (2)-(8) reaches the first outcome under the declared polynomial class.
